$comment: Machine-readable source of truth for the aggressive risk profile. Loaded by src/policy/schema.ts. Every value here is enforced in deterministic code; no LLM can widen any of it at runtime.

network.$comment_mainnet: base is deliberately absent. Enabling it requires a separate mainnet policy file plus a future explicit human enablement command. Three independent gates also check this.

capital.$comment_deployment: targetDeploymentBps is a REPORTING TARGET for the allocator. It is never an input to any quality gate. A system required to hit a deployment number opens bad trades to fill the quota. See docs/AGGRESSIVE-MODE.md 2.1.
capital.$comment_reserves: Wei retained for gas, never deployable. Also the floor below which deploying is pointless.

risk.$comment_daily: Drawdown is mark-to-market on open positions plus realised. A volatile book hits 8% on an ordinary alt flush, so the response is DE-RISK (block new risk, allow exits), not a blanket stop. See docs/AGGRESSIVE-MODE.md 2.2.

execution.$comment_edge: Gate on net expected edge after costs, not on a raw slippage cap. Tight slippage caps reject exactly the breakout entries this strategy wants. Absolute bounds remain as circuit breakers against a hostile pool. See docs/AGGRESSIVE-MODE.md 2.3.
execution.$comment_dust: Below this notional the gas and fee cost dominates and the edge calculation is noise.

assets.$comment_allowlist: Empty allowlist means 'not restricted to a list'. The denylist always applies regardless.
assets.$comment_guards: Structural safety checks the Scout/Risk agents must satisfy before a token is tradable at all.

exits.$comment: forceExitOnInvalidationBreach is a hard invariant: Big Pickle may exit early for any reason, but may never decline a forced exit. This is what makes max-loss enforceable.

concurrency.$comment: Aggressive rotation races the nonce. One signing slot, no parallelism in the signing path. See docs/AGGRESSIVE-MODE.md 3.4.

circuitBreaker.$comment: Any trip freezes trading until a human resumes. Sticky by design. See docs/AGGRESSIVE-MODE.md 3.3.

prediction.$comment: ADDITIVE section. Every limit here is new and additional; nothing in assets/execution/risk is relaxed to accommodate prediction instruments. The assets.* floors above are denominated for on-chain token pools (a $50k liquidity floor) and describe a structurally different instrument: a prediction contract has no pool, no holders and no honeypot. A prediction order against a policy WITHOUT this section is refused outright rather than evaluated against limits that do not exist.
prediction.$comment_survival: Calibrated for the $50 survival experiment. A $50 book cannot see $50,000 of depth, so the floors are denominated for contract books, not token pools. See docs/PREDICTION-MARKETS.md.
prediction.$comment_spread: 4% of the midpoint. Wider than a liquid crypto venue because prediction books are thin, and this is the single most effective cost gate in the whole engine.
prediction.$comment_edge: Net edge is return on cost AFTER fees, spread, slippage and the safety margin. 2.5% on a $50 book is real money, which is the point: most candidates must be refused to reach it.
prediction.$comment_safety: Haircut applied to the raw estimate for model error and data staleness. Charged before the edge test, not after, so it can never be netted out.
prediction.$comment_freshness: No entry on data older than 2 minutes. A prediction quote can gap while a 2-minute-old copy looks perfectly reasonable.
prediction.$comment_horizon: No entry within 30 minutes of resolution: the remaining edge cannot be earned and the fill is pure adverse selection.
prediction.$comment_premium: A binary contract settles or it does not. The true worst case is the whole premium, so this is checked against the full premium, independent of any stop the model imagines.
prediction.$comment_concentration: Four 'unrelated' contracts about the same election are one bet. Category and correlation-group caps exist for that reason.
prediction.$comment_confidence: Below this the estimate is noise dressed as a number.
prediction.$comment_kelly: Quarter Kelly. Full Kelly on an uncertain probability is the fastest way to a $50 account on the way to zero.

fees.$comment: takerFeeBps is floored at execution.assumedFeeBps by the schema, so the hard-limit engine's edge arithmetic can never be more permissive than the real fee. flatFeeMicrosPerContract models the per-contract schedules some venues use, charged IN ADDITION to the rate.
